 MAGA podcaster Katie Miller blames mothers for election disaster as she admits she didn't vote
 MAGA podcaster Katie Miller has blamed the midterm election results on mothers as she claimed that they failed to turn up at the polls, despite not casting a ballot herself
 Add to preferred sources Entertainment Caroline Gaspich Entertainment Reporter 11:24 ET, 04 Nov 2026 View 4 Images Katie Miller said that MAGA moms did not turn out to the polls for the midterm elections (Image: Getty Images) 
 MAGA podcaster Katie Miller blamed the Republican midterm loss on mothers not turning up at the polls.
 ‌ 
 ‌ 
 Miller, the wife of Donald Trump's advisor Stephen Miller, appeared on CBS News shortly after the midterm election results rolled in with Democrats winning both the Senate and House. As she attempted to explain the outcome, she called out busy MAGA mothers for not taking the time out of their busy schedules to cast their ballots.
 The 34-year-old said, "You see that moms are too busy raising their children and taking care of them to go to the polls." In response, Norah O’Donnell asked her, "You’re a busy mom of four; did you make it out to vote?"
 ‌ 
 READ MORE : Katie Miller posts Star Wars Halloween costume pic and gets trolled for caption READ MORE : Katie Miller slams 'gross' Natalie Harp bombshell that exposes 'reason for Trump loyalty' Miller and her husband Stephen, 41, have four children together, including their five-year-old daughter Mackenzie, four-year-old son Jackson, three-year-old son Hudson Monroe, and their five-month-old son Hawthorne Hayes.
 The Katie Miller Podcast host then confessed that she is part of the problem, as she didn't participate in the midterms, citing her desire to maintain her privacy. She said, "I did not vote in Virginia because in Virginia, because in Virginia when you vote, you dox your own address, and so I prefer my own safety and security over giving that up."
 View 4 Images Katie is the wife of Trump advisor Stephen Miller (Image: CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images) 
 ‌ 
 The former advisor to Elon Musk and his now-defunct Department of Government Efficiency also blamed “candidate quality” for the lack of Republican wins in this midterm election and argued that many of the politicians "weren't good options in the first place."
 Despite not exercising her right to vote in the midterms, the conservative podcaster did shoot off a number of controversial posts about the election online.
 ‌ 
 Taking to X on November 3, Miller wrote, "Election Day always makes me want to have more kids to cancel out the votes of the America-hating leftists. After all, conservatives have more babies."
 View 4 Images Katie confirmed that she also didn't vote in the midterm elections (Image: WireImage) 
 ‌ 
 Following Democrats securing the majority in both the House and Senate, Katie took to X, sharing a follow-up post about the possibility of Trump being impeached.
 The podcaster penned, "President Trump endured two impeachments and was then resoundingly re-elected. President Trump and his team faced years of unrelenting partisan investigations and witch hunts, with subpoena after subpoena."
 Miller added, "He was resoundingly re-elected. A notable difference is that during our last round of investigations we lacked the Presidency and the power of the federal government. Our team is more united than ever before, we are more prepared than ever before, and we believe in the cause more than ever before."
 She concluded, "Best wishes and good luck to the Democrats. This strategy will backfire, as history has already proven."
 View 4 Images Katie's husband Stephen said that Trump 'bled' for America and needs voters to participate in the midterms (Image: Getty Images) 
 As for her husband, the day before midterms, Stephen urged voters to turn out at the polls, saying they owe it to the president to support the Republican Party after he "saved" America.
 During an appearance on the Fox News program Hannity, Stephen said, "He saved America from a corrupt political class. He saved America from open borders. He saved America from countries that want the American way of life to end, from foreign adversaries, from domestic adversaries."
 He closed, "President Trump took a bullet for you; he bled for you; he faced life in prison for you. And what he needs from you tomorrow is your vote.”
